propositions: When JIRA_PAT environment variable is absent, the DC adapter falls back to anonymous access instead of failing with a named error, contradicting the documented security guarantee.

Settings resolution passes an empty string as the bearer token to the Jira client, which succeeds but causes the client to operate anonymously, producing misleading error messages about missing projects rather than authentication failure.
A missing credential produces a confusing error (HTTP 400: project does not exist) that misdirects operators to check project keys and permissions instead of the missing environment variable.
Client construction in build_client_from_settings must validate that JIRA_PAT is non-empty before passing it to the Jira client to prevent anonymous fallback.
Settings resolution must remain total (not raise on missing credential) to preserve Python 3.11 Protocol conformance checks via hasattr, with validation deferred to client construction.
A PAT present only in the config file must not satisfy validation, preserving the documented environment-only contract.
